papers.title: TeRed: Normal Behavior-Based Efficient Provenance Graph Reduction for Large-Scale Attack Forensics
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.method: Learns normal behavior patterns using unit tests, then uses the patterns for provenance graph reduction.
papers.reported_evaluation: Publisher abstract claims all attack-related information retained on five datasets without compromising detection/investigation; exact numerical reductions unavailable.
papers.guarantee: Empirical preservation claim; no universal losslessness theorem verified.
concerns: Normal-template coverage and contamination must be audited.
Unknown exact template identity and matching semantics.
Do not generalize from normal test coverage to maliciousness or harmlessness.
papers.adaptation: Use independently collected normal workload templates as a reversible ranking feature. Preserve original event IDs and temporal witnesses. Do not exempt every event of a normal executable.

papers.title: PDCleaner: A multi-view collaborative data compression method for provenance graph-based APT detection systems
papers.method: Combines global-semantic event deletion, behavior-preserving entity aggregation, and event-chain merging using Levenshtein similarity.
papers.reported_evaluation: Five realistic scenarios: 14.43x compression, 4.98% average semantic loss, up to 20.22% shorter model training and +0.051 F1.
papers.guarantee: Explicitly allows semantic loss; not an exact evidence-preserving algorithm as a whole.
concerns: Precise semantic-loss metric and aggregation denominator unavailable.
Similarity can collapse rare distinguishing malicious steps.
Training/inference compression consistency and attack-label use unverified.
papers.adaptation: Begin with reversible duplicate-event aggregation, retaining multiplicity, type, timestamps and source event IDs. Evaluate event/entity/chain ablations separately against downstream detection and witness preservation.

papers.title: MPCA: Constructing the APTs provenance graphs through multi-perspective confidence and association
papers.method: Merges semantically consistent parallel branches in process-connected subgraphs; evaluates subject-relation-object event confidence and event-to-alarm association to suppress benign dependencies and emphasize attack events.
papers.reported_evaluation: CADETS and TRACE; introduction reports reduction rate 44.16% higher, accuracy improved by 82%, and FPR reduced by 21% relative to previous work.
papers.guarantee: No formal semantics or temporal-reachability preservation guarantee verified. Relative percentage definitions not recovered.
concerns: Alarm seed selection must be separated from truth.
The word confidence does not establish calibrated attack probability.
Label supervision and hyperparameter selection are not available.
papers.adaptation: Keep local event suspiciousness separate from alarm/POI association. Use strict temporal paths to gate evidence association and retain parallel branches as expandable groups.

papers.title: FineGCP: Fine-grained dependency graph community partitioning for attack investigation
papers.method: Partitions entities into task-oriented execution units, learns GNN node representations, and aggregates similar units using Louvain communities.
papers.reported_evaluation: Atlas-DS and DARPA TC: attack nodes average 1.34 communities; 97% attack-node proportion inside attack-containing communities. Modularity/coverage/performance 0.68/0.77/0.94; runtimes 156.91s and 389.63s.
papers.guarantee: Community purity is not detector recall or precision. No proof verified that one selected community contains an entire attack.
concerns: Execution units differ from original process UUID ground truth.
POI community may omit remaining attack communities.
Training labels and transductive evaluation not verified.
papers.adaptation: Introduce reversible per-process activity segments as investigative context; preserve UUID-to-segment mapping and cross-segment edges. Never label every segment or community member malicious from one member.

papers.title: A multi-source log semantic analysis-based attack investigation approach
papers.method: Normalizes application and OS logs, refines graph entities, merges repeated events, drops unreachable and temporary-file nodes, then matches report-derived attack subgraphs through a GNN-based seven-stage investigation.
papers.reported_evaluation: Abstract reports precision +15.1%, recall +12.2%, investigation time reduced >60% with F1 decrease <2%; distinct comparisons cannot be reconstructed from abstract.
papers.guarantee: Retaining main structure is not proof of temporal witness or forensic evidence preservation.
concerns: Threat-report templates can leak the evaluated campaign.
Missing application telemetry is a substantive input limitation.
Temporary files can carry attack payloads or credentials.
papers.adaptation: Add source-aware event normalization only for real available telemetry. Require actual evidence for each stage and report unknown stages; never blindly prune temporary files.

papers.title: LinTracer: An efficient tracking system for cyberattack chains fusing entity and event semantics
papers.method: Linux auditing and compression feed backward causal analysis from an alarm. Local/global feature scores propagate backward to locate entries; ATT&CK entity-semantic tags propagate forward, followed by path-level analysis. Conclusion mentions K-SUMS clustering and linear-discriminant feature projection.
papers.reported_evaluation: About 64 million events across lab data (January 15–21, 2024; Ubuntu 16.04/SPADE) and DARPA Engagement 4. Setup calls the DARPA data not publicly available.
papers.guarantee: No universal attack-chain or tag-propagation correctness guarantee verified.
concerns: ATT&CK semantic tags are not event ground-truth labels.
Need exact label requirements for linear-discriminant projection.
Linux-specific features require explicit Windows/OPTC mapping.
papers.adaptation: Represent backward entry candidates and forward impact hypotheses separately. Require timestamp-valid original-event witnesses and typed tag transfer. Keep malicious actors, resources and context separate.
